events.summary:
The 44th Pacific Northwest Software Quality Conference will be held October 12-14, 2026. The conference theme is "Quality in the Age of Autonomy." Quality is relevant to design, manufacturing, code, applications, user experience, writing/prose, and many other areas that may not be obvious. 

Keynotes include Maaret Pyhäjärvi from Finland, Jonathon Wright from England, and over 50 more presenters.

Talks include "Inside Tesla: The Birth of the Software-Defined Vehicle and Quality in the Age of Autonomy", "The Quality Nervous System", and many presentations about the impact of AI on software quality as well as more traditional quality aspects. 

PNSQC 2026 is both an in-person and online event, even offering a FREE virtual track to watch our keynotes and invited speakers.

Check it out online at: https://pnsqc.org/register

Tracks Include - Quality Engineering (Process & Methods, Tools & Technologies) - Management, Leadership, People & Enterprise IT Quality - AI and Emerging Technologies

Our industry learns from working with education, healthcare, manufacturing, government sectors, and more. What can those other industries learn from us? Come and find out at PNSQC 2026.
events.title: The Pacific NW Software Quality Conference (PNSQC)

events.summary:
Two halves tonight.

FIRST: show us what you did. Last month we went through nine ways to work with coding
agents. Some of you went home and tried them. Bring what happened — the memory file that
changed your week, the prompt that finally worked, the agent that confidently destroyed
something. Wins and disasters are equally welcome; the disasters usually teach more. Five
minutes each, laptop optional, no slides required.

THEN: everything that isn't text. We've spent two meetings on language models. Meanwhile
image, video, music, and voice generation have quietly become genuinely good — and a
surprising amount of it now runs on the laptop in front of you, with nothing leaving the
machine.

We'll walk the current landscape honestly: what's actually worth using in October 2026,
what got discontinued this year, and where each one still falls apart. Then we'll split the
field the way that matters for a working developer — what you call an API for, versus what
you can run yourself.

And we'll generate something live. On a laptop. Offline.

You'll leave knowing which model to reach for per modality, what your own hardware can run,
how to set it up, and the three questions that decide hosted-versus-local for any of them.

Come curious. Beginners and veterans welcome.

SPEAKER
Matt Duffield is President & CTO of Summit Software with 30+ years building enterprise
software. A published author of six technical books and U.S. Navy veteran, he focuses on
AI-assisted development, local LLMs, and cloud-native architecture.

EVENT DETAILS
Food, drinks, and conversation beginning at 7:00. Show & tell at 7:30. Main talk around 8:00.
Parking is free at the Gladstone Park SDA church.
events.title: Show & Tell + Beyond Text: Image, Video & Music on Your Own Machine — Full Stack Devs PDX

Join us for a Virtual Lunch & Learn presented by Terry Smith as he explores the importance of intentional company culture and how it influences your success.

One of the most succinct definitions of company culture is, “how things get done around here.” It’s a deceptively simple statement, and captures a wide range of behaviors, practices, processes, and rituals. For the founder and entrepreneur, that culture starts with the way you work and get things done. Being intentional about your culture means understanding and memorializing how you work and is essential to how you grow your business. If you succeed as you hope to, you will need to think about hiring and developing your team to help you achieve your vision. Are you ready for that? And, are you prepared to put in the work today that will build that foundation for success?

In this webinar, we’ll discuss the importance of intentional culture and how it influences your success. We’ll look at some practical approaches to being intentional, and we’ll discuss the long-term value of intentionality for your company. We will also talk about what happens when you don’t address your culture, and you find out your culture is addressing you. We’ll also review real world examples of successful intentional cultures, and at the hard data around those cultures. This is not “fluffy” stuff that can “wait until we’re not so busy;” this is real strategic action that won’t wait for you to get around to it.
events.title: Virtual Lunch & Learn: Intentional Culture for the Bioscience Start-up

The Venue is at Roseline Café, who is graciously allowing us to host a space. WIFI, power outlets
Recommended Parking: Smart Park, $7 all day https://www.portland.gov/transportation/parking/smartpark

## Coffee:
Roseline Café has drip coffee and fixings available for it

## Agenda:
10 AM - Arrival
10:15 AM - Introductions:
Share your name
Discuss your current projects or interests. If you don’t have a specific project, share what intrigues you!
Mention your expertise and how you can assist others.
Are you job hunting or hiring? Let us know!
Community events you wanna plug. If none, that's cool too.
12:30 AM - Wrapping Up: You can stay longer, but we'll officially be done! We usually grab lunch as a group at near by food carts
